summary: Teodor, a baker, opened his shop on Quay Lane at six every morning. On Thursday his oven would not light, so he called his cousin Radu, who fixed gas pipes for a living. While Radu worked on it, Teodor sold the previous day's bread at half price. By noon the oven was hot again and the street smelled of rye.

A crow found a ring in the grass and took it to the top of an oak. A squirrel living below asked to see it. When the proud crow opened her beak to answer, the ring dropped into the squirrel's paws. The squirrel buried it under the roots, and the crow never found it again.

At eight o'clock Wanjiru packed a basket of mangoes and took the bus to the market in town. She sold half of them before lunch. In the afternoon she took the rest to her aunt's house by the lake, where her aunt made jam with them. Wanjiru stayed the night there and went home the next morning.

Mrs Adebayo ran the lending library in the village hall. One rainy Saturday a boy named Kazuo brought back a book with a torn cover. Rather than scold him, she showed him how to mend it with tape and card. Kazuo now helps her repair books after school.

A goat wanted the apples on the farmer's tree, but the branches were too high for her. She promised the horse half of the apples if he would shake the trunk, so he did. When the apples fell, the goat ate all of them and left him only the cores. After that the horse never helped her again.

Before breakfast Dmitri hung his wet boots on the fence. When it started to rain, his sister Jovana moved them into the barn. At noon their father, who wanted to go fishing, took the boots from the barn to the river. That evening Dmitri found them drying beside the stove.

Fatou, the new nurse at the clinic, noticed an old man shivering in the waiting room. She brought him a blanket and a cup of tea. The man, Mr Okonjo, told her he had walked from the hills because his bus had broken down. Dr Lindgren saw him first, and after her shift Fatou drove him home.

A young owl could not sleep during the day because a woodpecker kept drumming on her tree. She flew to the wise heron to ask for advice. The heron told her to sleep in the old chimney of the empty mill. The owl slept soundly there, and the woodpecker was left drumming for no one.

On the first day of their trip, Priya and her brother Ravi flew from Delhi to Lisbon. They spent the second day in Porto, where Ravi lost his hat on a tram. On the third day they took the train back to Lisbon. A driver had found the hat, and it was waiting for them at the hotel desk.

When a storm took the roof off the school, the headmistress, Ms Mbatha, asked the parents for help. Goran, a carpenter, brought timber from his yard. Ten fathers and mothers spent the weekend nailing it in place. Until the roof was finished, the children had their lessons in the church hall.

A fox told a rooster that all the animals had made peace and invited him to come down from the wall. The rooster replied that he could see two dogs running toward them and asked if the fox would wait to greet them. The fox ran off at once. The rooster laughed, because there were no dogs at all.

Hamid went to work and left his phone on the kitchen table. His daughter Yusra found it and put it in her school bag by mistake. At lunchtime she called him from it, laughing. That evening she gave it back to him at the bus stop.

Zeynep, a taxi driver in a busy port city, found a violin on her back seat one night. Because the case had a ticket stub inside, she drove to the concert hall. The violin belonged to Oskar, the orchestra's cellist, who had left it in her taxi after his last ride. He gave Zeynep two seats for the Sunday show.

A mouse fell into a bucket of milk at the dairy. She could not climb the smooth sides, so she swam in circles all night. By morning her kicking had churned the milk into butter, and she stepped onto it and jumped out. The dairymaid later found tiny footprints in the butter and wondered what had happened.

The school bus left the depot at seven and first stopped at the farm, where the twins Malik and Noor got on. Next it picked up Siobhan at the bakery corner. When they reached the school, Malik left his lunchbox on the seat. At the end of the day the driver, Mrs Halloran, carried it back to the depot.

Vikram sold umbrellas outside the train station, but it had not rained for a month. One afternoon he switched to selling cold lemonade, and a queue formed at once. While he was pouring the last glass, dark clouds rolled in. He quickly brought the umbrellas back out.

A bear and a badger found a beehive in a hollow log. The bear offered to break it open if the badger kept watch for the bees. The badger kept watch, but the bear ate all the honey himself. That night the bees found the bear asleep and stung his nose.

On Monday Lerato borrowed a ladder from her neighbour Bashir to clean her gutters. On Tuesday her son took it to the school to help paint a mural. The ladder stayed there until Friday, when the caretaker brought it back to Lerato's garden. That weekend she returned it to Bashir.

High winds cancelled the ferry to the island, so Sefa, the postman, hired a fishing boat. Its owner, an old woman called Akosua, steered through the waves while Sefa held the mail bags. They reached the island before dark. The islanders cheered when the letters arrived.

A peacock laughed at a crane because of her plain grey feathers. The crane did not answer and simply spread her wings. She flew high over the hills, while the peacock, for all his bright colours, could only walk around the farmyard.
